analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: the date bump at line 3 and a new documentation paragraph (head lines ~874-878, per the patch hunk) saying GLM prompt rendering now maps OpenRouter-returned assistant reasoning (`reasoning` / `reasoning_details`) to the template's `reasoning_content`, and that `strict` tools are served by validating each `auto` call against its schema via `ToolConstraintValidation.validate` rather than by constrained decoding. No code, configuration or threat-model YAML changes are in the supplied evidence. The supplied units are the BASE tail (lines 2366-2597) and the HEAD start (lines 1-415); neither contains the changed hunk text, so I could not read the exact edited lines. I verified the hunk only through the patch excerpt.

Security relevance: the docs describe code paths this PR did not supply, so I treated them as unverified contract. Replaying client-supplied prior-turn reasoning into the prompt is a prompt-content input channel. It relates to A-001 and to prompt-contract and normalization consistency with the coordinator sidecar (the Flint request-normalization note elsewhere in the file). The strict-tool validation statement is consistent with the existing fail-closed validation model, and it does not claim constrained decoding. No new trust boundary, authorization, attestation, encryption, billing or cache change is visible.

The cache and T-041 content in the file is unchanged context. The Flint, Nemotron and Bonsai sections are unchanged and were not re-evaluated as regressions.

Remaining questions for integration, if the code changes are in another batch: (1) whether `returnedReasoning` is bounded in size, sanitized and confined to assistant turns; (2) whether it affects the prompt-contract ID or cacheSalt scoping; (3) whether the coordinator's prompt sidecar mirrors the rendering. These cannot be judged from documentation alone. No finding is warranted from this documentation-only change.
